roleOnlyRemovals.note: semanticRole never appeared in the prompt text - it existed only as a schema field. That is consistent with both arms mismatching Gold's ontology on all 42 target claims: nothing ever told the model what vocabulary to use.

preservedMembershipContent.what: the document's own title and subtitle, running headers and footers, table and figure labels, form and signature labels are real labels and should still be reported
preservedMembershipContent.wasStatedIn: the parent-node:NONE paragraph of the base prompt
preservedMembershipContent.why: That sentence is membership wearing a placement token. Dropping the paragraph wholesale would have narrowed what the model accepts and turned a task decomposition into an unauthorized policy change.

requestAuthority.evidenceMeaning: The packet the harness builds from atoms, ownership, margins and layout, before the schema is appended. It also carries the contract's protocol version, so a Stage-1 packet cannot be byte-identical to a v2 one.
requestAuthority.evidenceProof: The packets are equal once the protocol field, and only the protocol field, is neutralised; they are unequal without that. So atoms, ownership, margins and layout did not move, and the difference is one declared string.
requestAuthority.honestyNote: Reporting this as byte-identical would repeat the mislabelling that already cost one preflight its lineage.
requestAuthority.userMessageNote: The composer appends SCHEMA= to the packet, so the user message differs from the baseline's by exactly the schema. The packet inside it is asserted identical.
requestAuthority.providerInputMeaning: system prompt and user message together, composed exactly as the adapter composes them when it reserves a capture slot

providerSettings.unavoidableDifference: none beyond the response schema itself
